$comment: Advisories accepted for now, one section per lock file (read by scripts/ci/audit.mjs, which the blocking audit job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs). Each entry maps an advisory id (GHSA-... or abandoned:<package>) to the reason it is accepted: no fixed release within the manifest ranges, not reachable, or a build or development tool only. In an npm section an entry is {"reason": ..., "via": [...]}: "via" lists the dependents the reason assumes, the packages through which npm audit reports the vulnerable package (its "effects"), and "(direct)" if the project itself depends on it. The audit fails when the advisory is reported through a dependent the entry does not list, so the reason is checked again before the list grows. A composer entry is the reason alone: composer audit names no dependents. Fix an advisory with a compatible update first; list it here only when that is not possible. The audit fails on an advisory that is not listed and on an entry or a dependent that no longer matches one, so an entry is removed as soon as its fix lands.

GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4.reason: glob (moderate). No fixed release within the manifest ranges: the advisory covers glob up to 14.0.1, but the Expo SDK 58 tooling (@expo/cli, @expo/config, @expo/config-plugins, @expo/fingerprint, @expo/metro-config) requires glob ^13 (13.0.6 is locked); npm's only offered fix is a breaking downgrade of expo. Build and development tool only: these packages find project files on the developer's or build machine (CLI, app config, prebuild, fingerprint, Metro configuration), with patterns from the project, never from a user or a request. The app's source does not import glob and neither server has it. Remove this entry with the Expo update that moves to a fixed glob (the audit then reports it as stale).

GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249.reason: minimatch (moderate). No fixed release within the manifest ranges: fixed in 11.0.1, but ESLint and its plugins (eslint, @eslint/config-array, @eslint/eslintrc, eslint-plugin-import, eslint-plugin-react: ^3.1; @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree: ^10.2.2) and the Expo tooling's glob 13 and @expo/fingerprint (^10.2.2) require older majors; npm offers no fix. Build and development tool only: ESLint runs on the developer's machine and in the CI lint job, the Expo packages on the developer's or build machine, and every pattern comes from the project's own configuration, never from a user or a request (the flaw needs a crafted pattern). The app's source does not import minimatch and neither server has it. Remove this entry with the updates that move to a fixed minimatch (the audit then reports it as stale).
